items.title: 67425_Tiny Grimes oral history interview
items.q: I mean you have to be like Jo Jones he's a drummer, man.

ctx.x: The record dates, they were all right. Cause we know what we were doing. Wasn't nobody nervous or no nothin' cause we were workin together all that time. No problem, you know. We didn't have a drum. And I wonder now how they kept such good tempo, good time 'cause we didn't have no drum. I guess that's why I'm so tough on drummers. They don't play the drums all the way. A lot of them play like they sprained their ankle, know what I mean? ~~Bass drum~~ like the bass drum-- foot hurt or somethin'. Now and then…

items.title: 68642_Jo Jones oral history interview
items.q: Art got the trio with Tiny Grimes.

ctx.x: Art got the trio with Tiny Grimes. Tiny Grimes had a little four-string guitar and he was scared to death. He hadn't been playing for about 9 months and he's sitting up there — But they was playing "The Streets of Paris". I said, "Cozy, you have to go."

And Fess came into the hotel on Central Avenue — and that's one of the first times in my life — you know, Cab Calloway, people don't know but Cab Calloway would work so much and do so many things off the stage, because Cab Calloway was doing so many civic things that people don't know nothing about. You know, it would take him 2 months and then if he's off for 2 or 3 days he'd get tore up. But then for the next two months he took care of business; he didn't mess around, because you know he didn't go for no…
